# Dimension 3: PA Integration Architecture

Reference file for the Todoist PA integration research.
See [citations.md](../citations.md) for source details.

## Task Signals for Advisory PA

The REST API's `GET /api/v1/tasks` accepts a `filter` parameter using Todoist's
filter syntax [1][7]:

| Signal | Filter Expression | Priority |
|--------|------------------|----------|
| Overdue tasks | `overdue` | High |
| Today's tasks | `today` | High |
| Combined urgency | `(today \| overdue)` | High |
| High-priority overdue | `p1 & overdue` | High |
| Upcoming (7 days) | `7 days` | Medium |
| Priority items | `p1`, `p2` | Medium |
| Project-scoped | `#ProjectName & today` | Context-dependent |
| Label-scoped | `@errands & (today \| overdue)` | Context-dependent |

Filter syntax uses `&` (AND), `|` (OR), `!` (NOT), `@` for labels, `#` for projects [7].

## Data Model Mapping

| Todoist Concept | PA Concept | Mapping Notes |
|-----------------|------------|---------------|
| Task | Action Item | Core unit; priority (1-4), due dates, duration [1] |
| Project | Context | Groups tasks (e.g., "Home", "Health", "Finance") [34] |
| Label | Category | Cross-project tagging (e.g., @errands, @phone) [34] |
| Section | Sub-context | Within-project grouping [1] |
| Filter | Dynamic View | Saved queries; 3 on Free, 150 on Pro [4] |
| Comment | Note/Detail | Attached to tasks or projects [1] |
| Reminder | Alert | Pro-only [4] |
| Duration | Time estimate | Amount + unit for time blocking [1] |

## Efficient "What Needs Attention" Query

A single API call retrieves the most actionable tasks:

```
GET /api/v1/tasks?filter=(today | overdue) & (p1 | p2)
```

This surfaces all high-priority tasks that are due today or overdue in one request [1][7].

For a comprehensive daily briefing, the PA should make 2-3 calls:
1. `filter=(today | overdue)` — everything needing attention now
2. `filter=7 days & p1` — upcoming high-priority items
3. `GET /api/v1/user/productivity_stats` — completion trends

At 3 calls per briefing, even hourly polling uses only 48 requests/day — well within the
1000/15min rate limit [10].

## MCP Server for PA

### Official (ai.todoist.net/mcp)

Best for:
- Hosted deployment (no infrastructure to manage) [14]
- Production use with OAuth-based auth [14]
- ChatGPT and other client compatibility [12][14]

Limitation: curated small tool set may lack granular queries [14].

### Community (greirson/mcp-todoist)

Best for:
- Self-hosted PA where you control the token [15]
- Granular access (19 tools covering all resource types) [15]
- Testing with dry-run mode [15]
- Activity logs and completed task retrieval [15]

### OAuth for Read-Only PA

The `data:read` scope restricts access to read operations only [3]. This is the correct
scope for an advisory PA that surfaces information without taking actions.

For a future write-capable PA (e.g., creating tasks from voice input), add `task:add` [3].

## Quick Add (Future Write Path)

`POST /api/v1/tasks/quick_add` parses natural language input, extracting dates, priorities,
labels, and project assignments [1]. The community MCP server exposes this as `todoist_task`
with `quick_add` action [15]. Syntax examples:

- "Buy groceries tomorrow #Shopping @errands p1"
- "Call mom {deadline in 3 days}"
- "Team meeting today at 2pm #Work @meetings"

[15]

## Rate Limit Assessment

| Usage Pattern | Requests/Hour | % of Limit |
|---------------|---------------|------------|
| Hourly briefing (3 calls) | 3 | 0.075% |
| 5-min polling (1 call) | 12 | 0.3% |
| 1-min polling (1 call) | 60 | 1.5% |
| Daily summary (10 calls) | 10/day | Negligible |

The 1000/15min limit is generous for any advisory PA pattern [10].

## Gaps and Limitations

- Free tier limits advisory PA: only 3 filter views and no reminders [4]
- No push notifications; PA must poll via Sync API or use webhooks [2][27]
- Official MCP server tool list not enumerated; may lack needed query tools [14]
- Filter syntax reference not fully extracted from source documentation [7]
